metadata.architecture: width-12 single causal attention residual with parameter-free normalization
metadata.mechanism_hypothesis: Twelve channels split across two attention heads can preserve operand routing and carry-state capacity while reducing embedding and attention parameters.
metadata.name: Width Twelve Routing Capacity Test
metadata.research_alternative_explanation: Addition may require two distinct routing heads but only six channels per head, making a twelve-channel state sufficient.
metadata.research_challenged_assumption: The current direction treats fourteen hidden channels as necessary for stable alignment and carry-sensitive prediction without decisive public evidence.
metadata.research_current_explanation: Two attention heads may provide the necessary routing separation, while the fourteen-channel representation may contain redundant arithmetic-state capacity.
metadata.research_decision_rule: Retain width twelve only if it passes validity and the frozen public robustness floor; otherwise restore the wider representation.
metadata.research_discriminating_evidence: Preserved eligibility would favor redundant channel capacity, whereas failure at width twelve would support a representational threshold above twelve channels.
metadata.research_evidence: The width-14 parent has 994 trusted parameters and a public search score of 0.000000, providing no decisive evidence that all fourteen channels are necessary.
metadata.research_expected_result: If routing and carry state are sufficiently low-dimensional, the candidate will preserve public eligibility with fewer trusted parameters.
metadata.research_next_experiment: Reduce the shared hidden width from fourteen to twelve while preserving two causal attention heads, residual routing, sinusoidal positions, parameter-free normalization, and tied readout.
metadata.research_previous_interpretation: The width-14 reduction lowered parameter count, but its zero public score does not demonstrate that fourteen channels provide essential computation capacity.
